title: Matching a variable name
description:
Environment strings look like `NAME=value`. Write two functions that help find one:

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `starts_with(text, prefix)` | 1 if the zero-terminated `text` begins with all of `prefix`, else 0 (an empty prefix always matches) |
| `value_length(text, name)` | if `text` is `name` followed by `=`, the length of the value after the `=`; otherwise −1 |

`value_length("HOME=/home/ada", "HOME")` is 9, but `value_length("HOMEPAGE=x", "HOME")` is −1.

starter.solution.asm:
starts_with:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

value_length:
        mov     rax, -1
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
starts_with:
.loop:  movzx   eax, byte [rsi]
        test    al, al
        jz      .yes
        cmp     al, [rdi]
        jne     .no
        inc     rdi
        inc     rsi
        jmp     .loop
.yes:   mov     eax, 1
        ret
.no:    xor     eax, eax
        ret

value_length:
.name:  movzx   eax, byte [rsi]
        test    al, al
        jz      .eq
        cmp     al, [rdi]
        jne     .no
        inc     rdi
        inc     rsi
        jmp     .name
.eq:    cmp     byte [rdi], '='
        jne     .no
        inc     rdi
        xor     eax, eax
.count: cmp     byte [rdi + rax], 0
        je      .done
        inc     rax
        jmp     .count
.no:    mov     rax, -1
.done:  ret

hints: Walk both strings while the prefix has characters left; the first mismatch means no (lesson 8.05).
For `value_length`, after the whole name matched, the next character must be `=`; then count until the zero byte.
unitTests:
test "prefixes"
    starts_with("PATH=/usr/bin", "PATH=") == 1
    starts_with("PATHEXT=.exe", "PATH=") == 0
    starts_with("abc", "") == 1
    starts_with("ab", "abc") == 0
test "values"
    value_length("HOME=/home/ada", "HOME") == 9
    value_length("HOMEPAGE=x", "HOME") == -1
    value_length("EMPTY=", "EMPTY") == 0
    value_length("HOME", "HOME") == -1
    value_length("X=1", "Y") == -1
